title: Calendars and Dates
introduction: Build on Primary 1 knowledge and practise calendars and dates.
definition: A calendar organises days into weeks, months and years. A week has seven days. Months have 28, 29, 30 or 31 days, depending on the month and whether it is a leap year.

formulas.expression: Inclusive day count = end day − start day + 1
formulas.description: For dates in the same month.

examples.question: How many days are in 3 weeks?
A holiday starts on 10 June and ends on 14 June, including both dates.

exercises.question: How many days are in 4 weeks?
How many months are in one year?
How many days are in April?
exercises.solution: April is one of the 30-day months, along with June, September and November.

exercises.question: How many days are in July?
exercises.solution: July is one of the 31-day months.

exercises.question: How many days from 5 May to 8 May, including both dates?
If today is Monday, what day is two days later?

summary: A calendar organises days into weeks, months and years. A week has seven days. Months have 28, 29, 30 or 31 days, depending on the month and whether it is a leap year.
